paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: nothing stays hidden, so don't live a double life. Jesus warns, "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy." (Luke 12:1) Leaven works its way through the whole batch of dough, and hypocrisy does the same to a heart. Then He says, "There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known." (Luke 12:2) So the safest way to live is the same way in the dark as in the daylight, and that is GOOD news, because you can quit holding up the act.

Now, why can a baker live that way? Because fear doesn't get the last word. Jesus tells His friends not to be afraid of those who kill the body, and He says to fear the One who has authority after that. (Luke 12:4-5) Then comes the tender part: "Yet not one of them is forgotten by God." (Luke 12:6) And Jesus says, "you are worth more than many sparrows." (Luke 12:7) The God who sees every hidden thing is the same God who keeps count of every hair on your head. I think that's why His eyes on you can bring peace instead of panic.

So what do you do with that? You stand up for Jesus out loud. He says whoever confesses Him before men, He will confess before the angels of God, and whoever denies Him will be denied. (Luke 12:8-9) And you don't have to find the words on your own, because "the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say." (Luke 12:12) Honest living, a steady heart and a bold word all come from knowing who has you. Hold on tight, baker, because this teaching isn't over.
